1.explanation: The YAML grammar definition lives in components/prism-yaml.js (and its minified counterpart). That file declares the patterns for strings and for comments. Currently the string regex doesn’t account for an inline “#” comment delimiter on the same line, so if a comment follows the closing quote, the string token is never matched. To fix it, you must adjust the string pattern (or its lookahead) in prism-yaml.js so that a double-quoted string is still recognized even when a # comment follows on that line. After updating the source, rebuild or regenerate the .min.js to apply the fix there as well.
1.bug_scenario:
When highlighting a YAML code block with Prism.js, any double-quoted string that has a comment on the same line (e.g. “\"world\" # test”) fails to be recognized and highlighted as a string. In the example, the second line’s “world” (without a trailing comment) is highlighted correctly, but the first one is not.

The supplied screenshot shows the first "world" in plain text (no string color), while the standalone second one is colored correctly.

2.explanation: Both prism-yaml.js and its minified counterpart define the grammar rules for YAML strings and comments in Prism. The string pattern in prism-yaml.js doesn’t allow for a trailing comment on the same line, so when a comment follows a quoted string the string rule fails to match and only the comment rule applies. Updating the regex for quoted strings in prism-yaml.js (and rebuilding the minified version) will fix the highlighting for YAML strings that have trailing comments.
2.bug_scenario: In Prism’s YAML language definition, quoted strings are not highlighted when there is an inline comment on the same line. In the provided example, the second item (“world”) without a trailing comment highlights correctly in green, but the first item with “# test” after it doesn’t get the string token and instead only the comment is tokenized. This shows that the YAML grammar in Prism doesn’t handle trailing comments after quoted strings correctly.
